{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019WRgCdFpYUCKBjwCVaLaVg","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Carepaths Inc — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.carepaths.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Carepaths Inc is a small, private behavioral health technology company based in Florida (Jupiter/Vero Beach), founded around 2000. The company was started by two psychologists who saw a role for technology in behavioral health practice; they initially developed an outcomes tracking system and then expanded into a full EHR. Barrett Griffith serves as CEO/CTO, having been named to the role after three years as CTO. The company has over two decades of experience in behavioral health software.\n     9→\n    10→CarePaths is a niche vendor focused exclusively on behavioral health — psychiatrists, psychologists, marriage and family therapists, counselors, addiction specialists, social workers, nurse practitioners, and training clinics. Their website reports processing over 8 million claims and 14 million patient appointments, with 805,000 assessments completed. The product is priced at $49/month per primary clinician, positioning it as an affordable option for solo practitioners and small-to-mid-size behavioral health practices. The company appears to be small (likely under 50 employees based on available signals), competing on affordability and behavioral-health-specific features rather than broad enterprise capabilities.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: CarePaths EHR\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 10607\n    15→Version: 19.11\n    16→Certification date: 2021-04-08\n    17→SED intended users: Behavioral Practitioners\n    18→\n    19→### What It Is\n    20→\n    21→CarePaths EHR is an all-in-one, cloud-based behavioral health EHR and practice management platform. It is not a component of a larger system — the certified module *is* the full product. The platform combines clinical documentation, practice management (scheduling, billing, claims), measurement-based care (outcomes tracking), teletherapy, a patient portal, and a patient-facing mobile app (CarePaths Connect) into a single integrated system.\n    22→\n    23→The product is certified for 20+ ONC criteria including clinical capabilities (CPOE for labs, demographics, family health history), transitions of care, patient portal (view/download/transmit), FHIR API access, and EHI export. It is *not* certified for public health reporting criteria or standalone e-prescribing criteria, though e-prescribing is offered through a DrFirst/Rcopia integration (at additional cost of $75 setup + $40/month per prescriber).\n    24→\n    25→### Users & Market\n    26→\n    27→**Target users**: Behavioral health practitioners — psychiatrists, psychologists, therapists (MFT, LPC), social workers, addiction specialists, nurse practitioners, and training clinics/supervisees.\n    28→\n    29→**Clinical settings**: Primarily solo practitioners and small-to-mid-size group practices in outpatient behavioral health. The supervisor/supervisee workflow support suggests use by training programs and practices with licensed/unlicensed clinician pairs.\n    30→\n    31→**Market position**: Small niche vendor in the behavioral health EHR space, competing on price ($49/month) and behavioral-health-specific functionality. Rated 4.3 stars across 46 reviews (per vendor website). Reviews on FindEMR indicate users from practices with 1-50 employees. Not a major enterprise vendor.\n    32→\n    33→**No notable large-scale deployments** were found in the research. The product appears oriented toward individual practitioners and small groups rather than large behavioral health organizations or health systems.\n    34→\n    35→### Modules & Functionality\n    36→\n    37→Based on vendor website, feature pages, and third-party review sites:\n    38→\n    39→**Clinical Documentation**\n    40→- Extensive library of clinical templates for intakes, progress notes, treatment plans, case management assessments, and outcomes assessments (vendor website, practice management page)\n    41→- Forms maker enabling users to edit templates or create custom clinical documents (vendor website)\n    42→- Smart note prepopulation: new progress notes auto-populated from previous patient entries (clinical documentation feature page)\n    43→- Batch document generation for group and family sessions (clinical documentation feature page)\n    44→- Supervisor review and co-signing workflow (clinical documentation feature page)\n    45→- AI-powered session summaries for generating clinical notes from teletherapy sessions (product page)\n    46→\n    47→**Measurement-Based Care (MBC) / Outcomes Monitoring**\n    48→- Automated weekly patient assessments delivered via patient portal or CarePaths Connect app (MBC product page)\n    49→- Library of standardized instruments across three categories (MBC product page):\n    50→  - Adult: GAD-7, PHQ-9, OQ-45, HAM-A, and 20+ others (anxiety, depression, PTSD, OCD, substance use)\n    51→  - Child: ADHD, autism spectrum screening, anxiety, behavioral assessments (YOQ, SCARED)\n    52→  - Special populations: postpartum depression (EPDS), eating disorders, geriatric depression, quality of life\n    53→- Results displayed as graphs at top of patient chart showing progress over time (MBC product page)\n    54→- Customizable assessment batteries with clinician-defined schedules and automatic reminders\n    55→- Aggregate reporting at clinician, program, clinic, and PRN level for quality improvement and benchmarking (vendor website)\n    56→- Tracks anxiety, depression, wellbeing, loneliness, medication adherence, patient confidence in therapist/treatment (mobile app page)\n    57→\n    58→**Practice Management / Scheduling**\n    59→- Calendar management for individual clinicians and group practices (practice management page)\n    60→- Patient self-scheduling via patient portal and mobile app (practice management page)\n    61→- Appointment reminders via email/text (product page)\n    62→- Support for multiple office locations and unlimited users (practice management page)\n    63→\n    64→**Billing, Claims & Accounting**\n    65→- Automated charge posting: completing a progress note or intake automatically posts charges and generates claims (clinical documentation page, vendor website)\n    66→- Claims generated in X12 format for electronic submission to payers (vendor website)\n    67→- Built-in claim validation rules to ensure clean claims (vendor website)\n    68→- Electronic remittance processing with auto-posting of insurance payments (vendor website)\n    69→- Credit card payment processing with auto-posting (vendor website)\n    70→- Patient accounting: posting of payments and adjustments, invoice/statement generation in customizable styles (vendor website)\n    71→- Integrated CPT coding with compliance updates (CPT billing feature page)\n    72→- Free insurance eligibility lookups (home page)\n    73→\n    74→**E-Prescribing**\n    75→- Integrated via DrFirst/Rcopia platform (mandatory disclosures page)\n    76→- Separate per-prescriber fee ($75 setup + $40/month) (product page)\n    77→- Medication monitoring capabilities (FindEMR)\n    78→\n    79→**Teletherapy**\n    80→- Built-in HIPAA-compliant video sessions supporting up to six front door\" for self-referrals and appointment booking (product page)\n    96→- Patients can search CarePaths network for nearby clinicians, verify insurance, and book appointments (web search results)\n    97→- Integrates secure messaging, teletherapy, scheduling, assessments, and payment\n    98→- Replaces the earlier \"CarePaths Online Therapy\" app (web search results)\n    99→\n Appointment reminder records (email/text)\n   142→- Faxed documents\n   143→- Direct messages (transitions of care)\n   144→\n   145→**Teletherapy data** (partially evidenced):\n   146→- Session records exist (sessions launched from patient chart), but it is **unclear whether video session recordings are stored** — the vendor does not explicitly describe recording/storing teletherapy video. AI session summaries suggest at minimum some session content is processed.\n   147→\n   148→**Patient portal / engagement data** (directly evidenced):\n   149→- Document viewing and signature records\n   150→- Online payment records\n   151→- Self-scheduled appointments\n   152→- Assessment completions via portal/app\n   153→\n   154→**Audit / system data** (directly evidenced):\n   155→- Audit logs (certified for (d)(2))\n   156→- Authentication records (MFA support)\n   157→- Emergency access logs\n   158→\n   159→**Gaps / uncertainties**:\n   160→- The vendor website does not mention lab results storage (as opposed to lab ordering), which is typical for behavioral health where lab work is less common\n   161→- No mention of imaging/radiology results storage\n   162→- No mention of allergy lists specifically, though this may be captured in intake forms\n   163→- No mention of immunization records\n   164→- No public health reporting data (not certified for (f) criteria)\n   165→- Whether teletherapy sessions are recorded and stored is unclear\n   166→\n   167→---\n   168→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. The company was started by two psychologists who saw a role for technology in behavioral health practice; they initially developed an outcomes tracking system and then expanded into a full EHR. Barrett Griffith serves as CEO/CTO, having been named to the role after three years as CTO. The company has over two decades of experience in behavioral health software.\n\nCarePaths is a niche vendor focused exclusively on behavioral health — psychiatrists, psychologists, marriage and family therapists, counselors, addiction specialists, social workers, nurse practitioners, and training clinics. Their website reports processing over 8 million claims and 14 million patient appointments, with 805,000 assessments completed. The product is priced at $49/month per primary clinician, positioning it as an affordable option for solo practitioners and small-to-mid-size behavioral health practices. The company appears to be small (likely under 50 employees based on available signals), competing on affordability and behavioral-health-specific features rather than broad enterprise capabilities.\n\n## Product: CarePaths EHR\n\nCHPL IDs: 10607\nVersion: 19.11\nCertification date: 2021-04-08\nSED intended users: Behavioral Practitioners\n\n### What It Is\n\nCarePaths EHR is an all-in-one, cloud-based behavioral health EHR and practice management platform. It is not a component of a larger system — the certified module *is* the full product. The platform combines clinical documentation, practice management (scheduling, billing, claims), measurement-based care (outcomes tracking), teletherapy, a patient portal, and a patient-facing mobile app (CarePaths Connect) into a single integrated system.\n\nThe product is certified for 20+ ONC criteria including clinical capabilities (CPOE for labs, demographics, family health history), transitions of care, patient portal (view/download/transmit), FHIR API access, and EHI export. It is *not* certified for public health reporting criteria or standalone e-prescribing criteria, though e-prescribing is offered through a DrFirst/Rcopia integration (at additional cost of $75 setup + $40/month per prescriber).\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Target users**: Behavioral health practitioners — psychiatrists, psychologists, therapists (MFT, LPC), social workers, addiction specialists, nurse practitioners, and training clinics/supervisees.\n\n**Clinical settings**: Primarily solo practitioners and small-to-mid-size group practices in outpatient behavioral health. The supervisor/supervisee workflow support suggests use by training programs and practices with licensed/unlicensed clinician pairs.\n\n**Market position**: Small niche vendor in the behavioral health EHR space, competing on price ($49/month) and behavioral-health-specific functionality. Rated 4.3 stars across 46 reviews (per vendor website). Reviews on FindEMR indicate users from practices with 1-50 employees. Not a major enterprise vendor.\n\n**No notable large-scale deployments** were found in the research. The product appears oriented toward individual practitioners and small groups rather than large behavioral health organizations or health systems.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website, feature pages, and third-party review sites:\n\n**Clinical Documentation**\n- Extensive library of clinical templates for intakes, progress notes, treatment plans, case management assessments, and outcomes assessments (vendor website, practice management page)\n- Forms maker enabling users to edit templates or create custom clinical documents (vendor website)\n- Smart note prepopulation: new progress notes auto-populated from previous patient entries (clinical documentation feature page)\n- Batch document generation for group and family sessions (clinical documentation feature page)\n- Supervisor review and co-signing workflow (clinical documentation feature page)\n- AI-powered session summaries for generating clinical notes from teletherapy sessions (product page)\n\n**Measurement-Based Care (MBC) / Outcomes Monitoring**\n- Automated weekly patient assessments delivered via patient portal or CarePaths Connect app (MBC product page)\n- Library of standardized instruments across three categories (MBC product page):\n  - Adult: GAD-7, PHQ-9, OQ-45, HAM-A, and 20+ others (anxiety, depression, PTSD, OCD, substance use)\n  - Child: ADHD, autism spectrum screening, anxiety, behavioral assessments (YOQ, SCARED)\n  - Special populations: postpartum depression (EPDS), eating disorders, geriatric depression, quality of life\n- Results displayed as graphs at top of patient chart showing progress over time (MBC product page)\n- Customizable assessment batteries with clinician-defined schedules and automatic reminders\n- Aggregate reporting at clinician, program, clinic, and PRN level for quality improvement and benchmarking (vendor website)\n- Tracks anxiety, depression, wellbeing, loneliness, medication adherence, patient confidence in therapist/treatment (mobile app page)\n\n**Practice Management / Scheduling**\n- Calendar management for individual clinicians and group practices (practice management page)\n- Patient self-scheduling via patient portal and mobile app (practice management page)\n- Appointment reminders via email/text (product page)\n- Support for multiple office locations and unlimited users (practice management page)\n\n**Billing, Claims & Accounting**\n- Automated charge posting: completing a progress note or intake automatically posts charges and generates claims (clinical documentation page, vendor website)\n- Claims generated in X12 format for electronic submission to payers (vendor website)\n- Built-in claim validation rules to ensure clean claims (vendor website)\n- Electronic remittance processing with auto-posting of insurance payments (vendor website)\n- Credit card payment processing with auto-posting (vendor website)\n- Patient accounting: posting of payments and adjustments, invoice/statement generation in customizable styles (vendor website)\n- Integrated CPT coding with compliance updates (CPT billing feature page)\n- Free insurance eligibility lookups (home page)\n\n**E-Prescribing**\n- Integrated via DrFirst/Rcopia platform (mandatory disclosures page)\n- Separate per-prescriber fee ($75 setup + $40/month) (product page)\n- Medication monitoring capabilities (FindEMR)\n\n**Teletherapy**\n- Built-in HIPAA-compliant video sessions supporting up to six participants (product page)\n- Launched directly from patient chart (teletherapy feature page)\n- Available on desktop, iOS, and Android (teletherapy feature page)\n- No separate login or third-party tool required\n\n**Patient Portal**\n- View and sign documents (patient portal page)\n- Pay invoices online (patient portal page)\n- Schedule appointments (patient portal page)\n- Secure messaging with therapist (patient portal page)\n- Complete assessments / MBC instruments (patient portal page, MBC page)\n- Access teletherapy sessions (patient portal page)\n\n**CarePaths Connect (Mobile App)**\n- Patient-facing mobile app (iOS/Android) released ~2022 (press release)\n- \"Digital front door\" for self-referrals and appointment booking (product page)\n- Patients can search CarePaths network for nearby clinicians, verify insurance, and book appointments (web search results)\n- Integrates secure messaging, teletherapy, scheduling, assessments, and payment\n- Replaces the earlier \"CarePaths Online Therapy\" app (web search results)\n\n**Reporting & Analytics**\n- Reporting on clinical, financial, demographic, and quality data (practice management page)\n- eCQM / MIPS / MACRA quality measure reporting (product page)\n- Aggregate outcomes reporting for quality improvement\n\n**Other**\n- Fax capability for sending saved clinical documents from the EHR (practice management page)\n- Data migration / integration tools for connecting with other EHRs (practice management page)\n- Direct messaging (provided in-house, no additional fees) (mandatory disclosures page)\n- Multi-factor authentication, encryption, audit controls, emergency access (mandatory disclosures page)\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features and functionality documented above, CarePaths EHR stores and manages:\n\n**Clinical data** (directly evidenced):\n- Patient demographics (certified for criterion (a)(5))\n- Family health history (certified for (a)(12))\n- Clinical documents: intake assessments, progress notes, treatment plans, case management assessments (clinical documentation page, vendor website)\n- Custom clinical forms created via forms maker\n- Diagnoses (reviews mention \"add diagnosis\")\n- Treatment goals (reviews mention treatment plans)\n- Medication data via DrFirst e-prescribing integration (mandatory disclosures page)\n- Lab/imaging orders (certified for CPOE (a)(2)/(a)(3), though behavioral health context means these are likely less central)\n\n**Outcomes / assessment data** (directly evidenced):\n- Standardized assessment responses (PHQ-9, GAD-7, OQ-45, etc.) collected over time\n- MBC tracking data: anxiety, depression, wellbeing, loneliness, medication adherence, therapeutic alliance metrics (mobile app page)\n- Longitudinal outcomes graphs per patient\n\n**Administrative / financial data** (directly evidenced):\n- Appointment/scheduling data and calendar records\n- Insurance information and eligibility verification results\n- Claims data in X12 format\n- Electronic remittance records\n- Patient accounting: charges, payments, adjustments, invoices, statements\n- Credit card payment records\n- CPT codes associated with services\n\n**Communication data** (directly evidenced):\n- Secure messages between patient and therapist (patient portal, messaging features)\n- Appointment reminder records (email/text)\n- Faxed documents\n- Direct messages (transitions of care)\n\n**Teletherapy data** (partially evidenced):\n- Session records exist (sessions launched from patient chart), but it is **unclear whether video session recordings are stored** — the vendor does not explicitly describe recording/storing teletherapy video. AI session summaries suggest at minimum some session content is processed.\n\n**Patient portal / engagement data** (directly evidenced):\n- Document viewing and signature records\n- Online payment records\n- Self-scheduled appointments\n- Assessment completions via portal/app\n\n**Audit / system data** (directly evidenced):\n- Audit logs (certified for (d)(2))\n- Authentication records (MFA support)\n- Emergency access logs\n\n**Gaps / uncertainties**:\n- The vendor website does not mention lab results storage (as opposed to lab ordering), which is typical for behavioral health where lab work is less common\n- No mention of imaging/radiology results storage\n- No mention of allergy lists specifically, though this may be captured in intake forms\n- No mention of immunization records\n- No public health reporting data (not certified for (f) criteria)\n- Whether teletherapy sessions are recorded and stored is unclear\n\n---\n","numLines":168,"startLine":1,"totalLines":168}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XXXvh2CtuYK2tLRit4T5rr","type":"tool_result","content":"5:  <title>CarePaths EHR B10 Export Format</title>\n29:  <meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"CarePaths EHR B10 Export Format\">\n36:  <meta name=\"twitter:title\" content=\"CarePaths EHR B10 Export Format\" />\n121:              \"name\": \"B10 export format\",\n122:              \"item\": \"https://carepaths.com/b10-export-format\"\n430:Remarketing tags may not be associated with personally identifiable information or placed on pages related to sensitive categories. See more information and instructions on how to setup the tag on: http://google.com/ads/remarketingsetup\n1177:<h1>B.10 EHI Export</h1>\n1180:\tCarePaths EHR includes the capability to perform individual and bulk exports of patient EHI information. Admin users with record management permissions can access the EHI export from the exports dropdown on the patient management overview. After selecting which patients to export, the system will return a single .zip file for each patient, containing the relevant files for that patient. This file will be presented to the admin user through the internal messaging system, and can be downloaded directly.\n1183:\tFor full patient population exports, please contact support or schedule the export for outside business hours. Running bulk exports can be resource heavy, and doing so during the day may affect ehr functionality. \n1186:<p>Files included in B.10 EHI Export (w/ naming scheme and file type):</p>\n1188: \t\t<p><strong>1</strong> CCD (Continuity of Care Document) in xml format (cda_PATIENT_NAME.xml)</p>\n1200: \t\t<p>Any other files included are document/image uploads from the patient's uploads on their EHR facesheet, in the same format as when uploaded</p>","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9203990a-9adc-4ea3-941a-a7bb9b53ce33","uuid":"f6762a0b-7c58-45b1-a7bb-ea46dcc7cf41","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"5:  <title>CarePaths EHR B10 Export Format</title>\n29:  <meta property=\"og:title\" content=\"CarePaths EHR B10 Export Format\">\n36:  <meta name=\"twitter:title\" content=\"CarePaths EHR B10 Export Format\" />\n121:              \"name\": \"B10 export format\",\n122:              \"item\": \"https://carepaths.com/b10-export-format\"\n430:Remarketing tags may not be associated with personally identifiable information or placed on pages related to sensitive categories. See more information and instructions on how to setup the tag on: http://google.com/ads/remarketingsetup\n1177:<h1>B.10 EHI Export</h1>\n1180:\tCarePaths EHR includes the capability to perform individual and bulk exports of patient EHI information. Admin users with record management permissions can access the EHI export from the exports dropdown on the patient management overview. After selecting which patients to export, the system will return a single .zip file for each patient, containing the relevant files for that patient. This file will be presented to the admin user through the internal messaging system, and can be downloaded directly.\n1183:\tFor full patient population exports, please contact support or schedule the export for outside business hours. Running bulk exports can be resource heavy, and doing so during the day may affect ehr functionality. \n1186:<p>Files included in B.10 EHI Export (w/ naming scheme and file type):</p>\n1188: \t\t<p><strong>1</strong> CCD (Continuity of Care Document) in xml format (cda_PATIENT_NAME.xml)</p>\n1200: \t\t<p>Any other files included are document/image uploads from the patient's uploads on their EHR facesheet, in the same format as when uploaded</p>","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

Admin users with record management permissions can access the EHI export from the exports dropdown on the patient management overview. After selecting which patients to export, the system will return a single .zip file for each patient, containing the relevant files for that patient. This file will be presented to the admin user through the internal messaging system, and can be downloaded directly.\n\t<br />\n\t<br />\n\tFor full patient population exports, please contact support or schedule the export for outside business hours. Running bulk exports can be resource heavy, and doing so during the day may affect ehr functionality. \n</p>\n\n<p>Files included in B.10 EHI Export (w/ naming scheme and file type):</p>\n\t<div style=\"padding-left: 10px;\">\n \t\t<p><strong>1</strong> CCD (Continuity of Care Document) in xml format (cda_PATIENT_NAME.xml)</p>\n\n \t\t<p><strong>1</strong> Accounting Statement listing Patient's accounting transactions (PATIENT_ID_Statements_asOfDate.pdf)</p>\n\n \t\t<p><strong>1</strong> Messaging History file of messages sent/received by Patient (PATIENT_ID_Message_History_asOfDate.txt)</p>\n\t\n \t\t<p>Patient Charts documenting completed service documents grouped by year (PATIENT_ID_Chart_Year.pdf)</p>\n\n\t\t<p>Audit Logs related to changes made to patient chart/account</p>\n\n\t\t<p> Appointment History and Statuses for the patient </p>\n\n \t\t<p>Any other files included are document/image uploads from the patient's uploads on their EHR facesheet, in the same format as when uploaded</p>\n\t</div>\n</div>\n</div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n    \n    \n      <div class=\"bg-cyan-200\">  \n  <div class=\"max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_012pwsRWQfmTKjiteRakMtfT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_015juspVjpKFVdtimB49nyuY","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/carepaths-inc--carepaths-ehr/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Carepaths Inc — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://carepaths.com/features/onc-certification/b10-export-format/\n- CHPL IDs: 10607\n- Product: CarePaths EHR v19.11\n- Certification date: 2021-04-08\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD request to the registered URL:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sI -L \"https://carepaths.com/features/onc-certification/b10-export-format/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: HTTP 200, content-type `text/html`, 93,196 bytes. No redirects.\n\n2. **Fetched and examined page content:**\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://carepaths.com/features/onc-certification/b10-export-format/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/b10-export-format.html\n   ```\n   The page is static HTML (not a SPA). The main content is in a `<div class=\"prose\">` block at lines 1177–1201 of the HTML. No JavaScript rendering required.\n\n3. **Searched for downloadable files** — no PDF, ZIP, XLSX, CSV, JSON, XSD, or other downloadable artifacts linked from this page. The page contains only prose text describing the export.\n\n4. **Checked related pages:**\n   - `/features/onc-certification` — lists certified criteria. The (b)(10) entry links back to the same B10 export format page. No additional export documentation.\n   - `/api-documentation` — 309 KB page documenting the FHIR (g)(10) API (patient-facing REST API). This is the g(10) standardized API, not the b(10) EHI export mechanism. Contains organization FHIR API URLs and FHIR resource documentation. Not relevant to EHI export.\n\n5. **Took screenshots** of the full page in the browser for archival purposes.\n\nNo additional linked documentation, downloadable files, data dictionaries, sample exports, or schema files were found anywhere on the carepaths.com site related to the (b)(10) EHI export.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single web page (~25 lines of prose) at the registered URL. It describes:\n\n### Export Mechanism\n- Admin users with \"record management permissions\" access the EHI export from the \"exports dropdown\" on the patient management overview.\n- Users select which patients to export.\n- The system produces a single `.zip` file per patient containing the relevant files.\n- The ZIP is delivered through the internal messaging system and can be downloaded directly.\n- For full patient population (bulk) exports, users must contact support or schedule outside business hours due to resource impact.\n\n### Files Included in the Export\n\nThe documentation lists 7 categories of files in each patient's ZIP:\n\n| # | File | Format | Naming Convention |\n|---|------|--------|-------------------|\n| 1 | CCD (Continuity of Care Document) | XML (CDA) | `cda_PATIENT_NAME.xml` |\n| 2 | Accounting Statement | PDF | `PATIENT_ID_Statements_asOfDate.pdf` |\n| 3 | Messaging History | TXT | `PATIENT_ID_Message_History_asOfDate.txt` |\n| 4 | Patient Charts (completed service documents, grouped by year) | PDF | `PATIENT_ID_Chart_Year.pdf` |\n| 5 | Audit Logs (changes to patient chart/account) | (format unspecified) | (naming unspecified) |\n| 6 | Appointment History and Statuses | (format unspecified) | (naming unspecified) |\n| 7 | Document/image uploads from the patient's facesheet | Original format | Original format as uploaded |\n\nThere is no data dictionary, no field-level documentation, no schema files, no sample exports, and no worked examples.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nCarePaths EHR is a behavioral health EHR storing clinical documentation (intakes, progress notes, treatment plans), standardized assessments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, OQ-45, etc.), billing/claims data, messaging, scheduling, and patient-uploaded documents.\n\n**What appears to be covered:**\n- **Clinical documentation** — via the CCD (CDA XML) and the Patient Charts PDFs. The CCD would capture structured clinical data (demographics, problems, medications, allergies, vitals). The chart PDFs presumably contain rendered copies of progress notes, intake assessments, and treatment plans.\n- **Billing/accounting** — the Accounting Statement PDF covers patient-level financial transactions (charges, payments, adjustments).\n- **Messaging** — the Message History TXT file captures patient-provider secure messages.\n- **Appointments** — appointment history and statuses are included.\n- **Document uploads** — patient-uploaded documents and images are included in original format.\n- **Audit logs** — included (though note: audit logs are not EHI per the designated record set definition, so their inclusion is a bonus).\n\n**What appears to be missing or uncertain:**\n- **Outcomes/assessment data (MBC)** — CarePaths' core differentiator is measurement-based care with dozens of standardized instruments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, OQ-45, HAM-A, SCARED, etc.) and longitudinal tracking. There is no mention of assessment response data in the export. The CCD likely does not include raw assessment scores and longitudinal tracking data. This is a significant gap — these are clinical records used to make treatment decisions.\n- **Treatment plans and goals** — While these may be captured in the chart PDFs as rendered documents, the structured data (goal status, target dates, interventions) would be lost in PDF rendering.\n- **Diagnoses as structured data** — The CCD should capture active diagnoses, but the completeness of diagnosis history (including resolved diagnoses, date ranges, and associated metadata) is unclear.\n- **E-prescribing / medication data** — Medication data in the CCD would be limited to whatever CarePaths stores locally. The DrFirst/Rcopia integration data (prescription history, medication monitoring) may or may not be included.\n- **Claims data (X12)** — The accounting statement is a PDF summary. Whether the underlying X12 claims, remittance records, and payment details are exported as structured data is unclear — a PDF statement is a significant downgrade from the structured billing records the system maintains.\n- **Insurance/enrollment information** — Not specifically mentioned.\n- **Supervisor/supervisee workflow data** — Notes requiring co-signatures, review status, supervision notes — likely rendered in chart PDFs but structural metadata would be lost.\n\n**The fundamental problem: PDF rendering destroys data fidelity.** The export strategy of rendering clinical documentation into annual PDF compilations means that structured clinical data (diagnoses with ICD codes, CPT codes on services, assessment scores, treatment plan goals with status tracking) is flattened into human-readable documents. A third party could read the PDFs but could not computationally process, query, or import this data into another system.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n- **CCD/CDA XML**: A recognized HL7 standard, but CDA is designed for clinical summaries, not comprehensive data export. A CCD typically covers demographics, problems, medications, allergies, vitals, procedures, and results — essentially the same USCDI/US Core data that (g)(10) covers. It would not capture behavioral health assessments, custom forms, or detailed billing records.\n- **PDF**: Not a computable format. Accounting statements, chart compilations, and audit logs as PDFs cannot be imported into another system without manual re-entry or OCR.\n- **TXT**: Messaging history as plain text is minimally computable — it preserves content but likely loses metadata (timestamps, sender identification, read status).\n- **Original format uploads**: Appropriate — returning documents in their original format is correct.\n\nThis export is essentially a **print-to-file** approach rather than a structured data export. The CCD provides some structured clinical data, but the remainder is PDFs and text files. This is a common pattern among small vendors — it satisfies the letter of the regulation (data is exported) but not the spirit (data should be usable).\n\n### The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Question\nThis vendor has NOT simply repackaged their FHIR API as the (b)(10) export. The export is a distinct mechanism (ZIP file per patient via the admin UI). However, the CCD XML component of the export covers roughly the same clinical data scope as the (g)(10) FHIR API would — structured clinical summaries — while everything else is rendered as PDFs. The export goes beyond clinical data (billing, messaging, appointments, uploads), but does so in non-computable formats.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n- **Extremely minimal.** The entire documentation is ~25 lines of prose on a single web page.\n- **No data dictionary.** There is no field-level documentation for any of the exported files.\n- **No schema or format specification.** The CCD is described as \"CDA XML\" but there's no indication of which CDA template, what sections are included, or what coded values are used.\n- **No sample exports.** No example files are provided.\n- **No import guidance.** A developer receiving this export would not know the structure of the CCD, the format of the audit logs, or the layout of the messaging history file without reverse-engineering actual exports.\n- **Two of the seven file categories don't even specify their format** (audit logs and appointment history).\n- **Incomplete naming conventions.** The naming scheme is provided for 4 of 7 file types.\n- **Could a developer implement an import?** No. The documentation is insufficient for a third party to build an automated import of this data. They could display the PDFs and parse the CCD with a generic CDA parser, but the behavioral health-specific data (assessments, treatment plans) would require manual extraction from PDFs.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n- **Granularity:** File-type level only. No table names, field names, data types, value sets, or relationships documented.\n- **Coded fields:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented.\n- **Versioning:** None visible. Page copyright says 2023.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://carepaths.com/features/onc-certification/b10-export-format/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML, no JS rendering needed)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered. The page loaded cleanly via curl and browser.\n- The page contains no downloadable files, no links to external documentation, and no links to further detail pages about the export.\n- The `/api-documentation` page documents the FHIR (g)(10) API only — not relevant to the (b)(10) EHI export.\n- The `/features/onc-certification` page links back to the same B10 export format page with no additional context.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":228,"cache_read_input_tokens":50749,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":228},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9203990a-9adc-4ea3-941a-a7bb9b53ce33","uuid":"39a556db-8832-4d3a-b02c-23fdeb2a4744"}

Accounting statements, chart compilations, and audit logs as PDFs cannot be imported into another system without manual re-entry or OCR.\n- **TXT**: Messaging history as plain text is minimally computable — it preserves content but likely loses metadata (timestamps, sender identification, read status).\n- **Original format uploads**: Appropriate — returning documents in their original format is correct.\n\nThis export is essentially a **print-to-file** approach rather than a structured data export. The CCD provides some structured clinical data, but the remainder is PDFs and text files. This is a common pattern among small vendors — it satisfies the letter of the regulation (data is exported) but not the spirit (data should be usable).\n\n### The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Question\nThis vendor has NOT simply repackaged their FHIR API as the (b)(10) export. The export is a distinct mechanism (ZIP file per patient via the admin UI). However, the CCD XML component of the export covers roughly the same clinical data scope as the (g)(10) FHIR API would — structured clinical summaries — while everything else is rendered as PDFs. The export goes beyond clinical data (billing, messaging, appointments, uploads), but does so in non-computable formats.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n- **Extremely minimal.** The entire documentation is ~25 lines of prose on a single web page.\n- **No data dictionary.** There is no field-level documentation for any of the exported files.\n- **No schema or format specification.** The CCD is described as \"CDA XML\" but there's no indication of which CDA template, what sections are included, or what coded values are used.\n- **No sample exports.** No example files are provided.\n- **No import guidance.** A developer receiving this export would not know the structure of the CCD, the format of the audit logs, or the layout of the messaging history file without reverse-engineering actual exports.\n- **Two of the seven file categories don't even specify their format** (audit logs and appointment history).\n- **Incomplete naming conventions.** The naming scheme is provided for 4 of 7 file types.\n- **Could a developer implement an import?** No. The documentation is insufficient for a third party to build an automated import of this data. They could display the PDFs and parse the CCD with a generic CDA parser, but the behavioral health-specific data (assessments, treatment plans) would require manual extraction from PDFs.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n- **Granularity:** File-type level only. No table names, field names, data types, value sets, or relationships documented.\n- **Coded fields:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented.\n- **Versioning:** None visible. Page copyright says 2023.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://carepaths.com/features/onc-certification/b10-export-format/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML, no JS rendering needed)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered. The page loaded cleanly via curl and browser.\n- The page contains no downloadable files, no links to external documentation, and no links to further detail pages about the export.\n- The `/api-documentation` page documents the FHIR (g)(10) API only — not relevant to the (b)(10) EHI export.\n- The `/features/onc-certification` page links back to the same B10 export format page with no additional context.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
